<!-- All news items below this line -->
;Armed conflicts and attacks
*A [[car bomb|motorcycle bomb]] explodes in front of a hotel in [[Spin Boldak]], [[Kandahar Province]], [[Afghanistan]]. Seven are wounded. [https://www.hindustantimes.com/world-news/7-injured-after-bomb-laden-motorbike-explodes-in-afghanistan/story-awtrPHlufmoUfOjg2YoS7J.html (''Hindustan Times'')]
*The [[Afghan National Army|Afghan army]], together with its international partners, launch a series of [[counterterrorism]] [[airstrike]]s in [[Kandahar]], [[Uruzgan]] and [[Zabul]], killing 58, including a [[Taliban]] governor. Ten mines are also destroyed. [https://www.hindustantimes.com/world-news/airstrikes-in-southeast-afghanistan-kill-47-terrorists-afghan-military-spokesperson/story-ScvIHdN8oHwqkV8eHvaUQL.html (''Hindustan Times'')]
*[[Syrian peace process]]
**The first meeting of the [[Syrian Constitutional Committee]] takes place in [[Geneva]] in a bid to end [[Syria|the country's]] eight-year-long [[Syrian Civil War|civil war]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-syria-security-un/syria-constitutional-panel-launched-amid-scepticism-idUSKBN1X919S?feedType=RSS&feedName=worldNews&&rpc=401 (Reuters)]

;Business and economics
*[[Twitter]] announces it will ban all political ads on its platform starting November 22. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-us-canada-50243306 (BBC News)]
*A man, 66-year-old Coy Featherson, homeless for 20 years, finds a permanent home, with the help of friends who had known him since middle school. [https://people.com/human-interest/friends-locate-homeless-childhood-pal/ (People)]

;Disasters and accidents
*[[2013 Glasgow helicopter crash]]
**The [[fatal accident inquiry]] into the crash concludes with the issuing of a report by Sheriff Principal Craig Turnbull. Turnbull criticises the helicopter's pilot, prompting concerns by some victims over excessive blame being placed upon [[pilot error]]. The aircraft crashed into a bar after running out of fuel. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-scotland-glasgow-west-50220838 (BBC News)]
*A fire destroys much of the 500-year-old [[Shurijo|Shuri Castle]] in [[Shuri, Okinawa]], [[Japan]], which is a [[United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization|UNESCO]] [[World Heritage Site]]. [https://www3.nhk.or.jp/nhkworld/en/news/20191031_09/ (NHK World-Japan)]

;Law and crime
*[[2019 Samoa assassination plot]]
**After months of delay, the [[Supreme Court of Samoa]] accepts a closed court bail hearing for two [[defendant]]s accused of attempting to [[assassinate]] [[Prime Minister of Samoa]] [[Tuilaʻepa Saʻilele Malielegaoi|Tuilaepa Sailele Malielegaoi]]. A third defendant who pleaded guilty is due to be sentenced on November 1. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/402127/samoa-s-highest-court-approves-closed-bail-hearing (Radio New Zealand)]
*[[Murder of Aya Maasarwe]]
**A court in [[Australia]] sentences Maasarwe's confessed killer, Codey Herrmann, to 36 years in prison with [[parole]] eligibility after 30 for [[rape]] and [[murder]]. The case prompted widespread debate about [[violence against women]] in Australia. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-australia-50216172 (BBC News)]
*[[2019 Chilean protests]]
**Due to the escalation in the protests, [[President of Chile|President]] [[Sebastián Piñera]] announces the cancellation of the [[APEC Chile 2019|2019 APEC Summit]] and the [[2019 United Nations Climate Change Conference|United Nations Climate Change Conference]], due to be hosted in Santiago in the following weeks. [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2019-10-30/chile-cancels-apec-summit-in-santiago-amid-wave-of-protests (Bloomberg)]
*[[Death of Jeffrey Epstein]]
**Dr. [[Michael Baden]], a [[medical examiner]] who observed the [[autopsy]] of [[Jeffrey Epstein]], says that it shows signs consistent with [[homicide]]. [https://www.yahoo.com/entertainment/famed-forensic-pathologist-dr-michael-151656473.html (Yahoo! News)]
*[[Crime in California]]
**A [[mass shooting]] at a [[Halloween]] [[costume party|party]] at a residence in [[Long Beach, California]], by at least one gunman, who is believed to have targeted the party but to have fired at random, kills three and injures at least nine, with some having significant injuries. [https://www.msn.com/en-us/news/us/3-dead-9-hurt-in-long-beach-shooting/ar-AAJz2jC?ocid=spartanntp (MSN)] 
*[[Censorship in Myanmar]]
**A court in [[Yangon]] convicts five members of satirical [[thangyat]] troupe Peacock Generation over an April performance in which they lampoon the nation's military. They each are jailed for one year. [http://bbc.co.uk/news/world-asia-50238031 (BBC News)]

;Sports
*[[2019 World Series]]
** The [[Washington Nationals]] beat the [[Houston Astros]] 6–2 in Game 7 to win the World Series. It is the franchise's first World Series championship and the first World Series victory for an MLB team based in the district since the [[History of the Washington Senators (1901–1960)|Washington Senators]] (now known as the [[Minnesota Twins]]) won in [[1924 World Series|1924]]. This World Series is also notable as the first in which all games were won by the [[Road (sports)|visiting team]]. [https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/mlb/playoffs/2019/10/31/washington-nationals-world-series-houston-astros/4105149002/ (''USA Today'')]
